# Dataset

## Summary

A schema-less table card: any screenshot, CSV, or pasted grid becomes one of these, whatever its columns — so ad-hoc data never needs its own CardDef. Columns and rows are stored as JSON strings (`columnsJson` is `[{ name, type }]` with type `string | number | date`; `rowsJson` is `[{ column: value, … }]`), parsed defensively by the exported `parseColumns` / `parseRows` helpers (malformed JSON yields `[]`, never a crash). Every dataset carries its provenance: `sourceNote` is a human-readable origin line whose leading vocabulary drives the provenance badge via the exported `provenanceKind` — `web-sourced …` (live search results), `… AI-recalled …` (model memory), anything else (a file the user dropped) — and `sourceFileUrl` links back to the original file written into the realm. The isolated view is a full data-table place: title, provenance badge, row/column counts, column-type chips, a sticky-header scrollable table with right-aligned numeric columns. The embedded view shows the badge, the count, and the first 12 rows with a "+N more rows" line.

ChartCards reference a Dataset via `linksTo`, so one dataset can feed several charts and a chart's data can be inspected on its own card.

## Import

```js
import { Dataset, parseColumns, parseRows, provenanceKind } from '../dataset';
```

## Usage

```js
new Dataset({
  title: 'Tesla 2025 quarterly deliveries',
  columnsJson: JSON.stringify([
    { name: 'quarter', type: 'string' },
    { name: 'deliveries', type: 'number' },
  ]),
  rowsJson: JSON.stringify([
    { quarter: 'Q1', deliveries: 336681 },
    { quarter: 'Q2', deliveries: 384122 },
  ]),
  sourceNote: 'web-sourced: quarterly press releases',
  sourceFileUrl: 'https://…/sources/deliveries.csv',
});
```

`sourceFileUrl` stays a plain string because a raw realm file write returns a URL, not a card id. Keep `rowsJson` within the 512KB realm card budget — the dashboard's ingestion paths cap rows for you and say so when they do.
